messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] p99 TLS handshake latency spike detected in eu-west-2 streaming ingress. p99 = 1.3s (SLO breach). Affected routes: /v1/stream, /v1/chat/stream. Paging on-call.

jessica: paging @raj — saw the bot. starting triage. carla, any customer-facing tickets yet?

carla: just one high-volume customer (acme-corp) reporting stream timeouts ~5m ago. support muted pings to avoid duplicates, forward logs attached.

raj (oncall): on it. quick health checks: streamer-frontend p95 looks ok, tail and handshake p99 is the outlier. suspect NAT/egress stalls or cross-AZ routing.

mike (neteng): running quick tcpdump on egress path for eu-west-2 nat-gw. grabbing SYN/ACK RTTs and retransmits.

mike (neteng): tcpdump snippet:
```
11:02:15.123456 IP 10.0.3.5.34567 > 54.12.34.56.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240
11:02:15.125987 IP 54.12.34.56.443 > 10.0.3.5.34567: Flags [S.], seq 67890, ack 12346, win 29200
11:02:15.125990 IP 54.12.34.56.443 > 10.0.3.5.34567: Flags [P.], seq ...  ack ...
11:02:16.340120 IP 10.0.3.5.34567 > 54.12.34.56.443: Flags [R.]
```
Looks like SYN/ACKs are delayed ~2x in some flows and occasional RSTs.

jessica: any DNS errors? TLS handshakes often follow DNS backoff in the chain.

mike (neteng): resolved no consistent DNS errors at resolver level, but seeing bursty retransmits on nat-gw telemetry and SNAT port exhaustion counters rising. running `netstat -s` and SNAT metrics now.

raj (oncall): can we confirm NAT SNAT port utilization? if ephemeral ports exhausted we get handshake failures. sophia, can platform-side autoscaling for nat-gw be bumped or do we fail open?

sophia (platform): autoscale settings are conservative to avoid cross-zone surfacing, but we can trigger an emergency scale + increase ephemeral port pool for the cluster. prepping a quick action: `infra runbook -> nat-gw emergency scale` (manual).

jessica: while that runs, let's reduce streaming concurrency per-connection to buy headroom. Patch proxy config to limit keepalive concurrency to 8 for eu-west-2. I'll push a canary.

deploy-bot: deploy started by jessica: patch stream-proxy (eu-west-2) -> limit.keepalive=8 (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%).

mike (neteng): SNAT stats snapshot:
```
snat_total_ports: 65536
snat_in_use_peak_1m: 48200
snat_in_use_current: 51900
snat_alloc_errors_5m: 12
```
We are near high watermark. That explains ephemeral collisions and extra handshake RTTs.

raj (oncall): urgent mitigation plan: 1) scale nat-gw pool by +30% (sophia), 2) shift 20% streaming traffic to eu-west-1 fallback (jessica), 3) enable short-lived connection reuse settings on clients (carla to coordinate support docs).

sophia (platform): executing scale up now. command: `infra nat-gw scale --region eu-west-2 --add 4`

sophia (platform): also applying ephemeral port range bump: `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 15000 65535` on nat instances via orchestration. rolling 2 at a time.

jessica: traffic shift command queued: `router adjust --service streamer --region eu-west-2 --shift 20% --to eu-west-1` executing staged rollout. will monitor errors/latency.

mike (neteng): after first nat-gw scaled instance came up, saw SNAT in_use drop to ~42000 and handshake p99 drop to ~800ms in canary flows. good sign.

carla: emailed acme-corp with interim mitigation note: "We are aware of increased stream timeouts in EU region; we have mitigations in flight and will update in 15m." they acknowledged.

raj (oncall): quick health check commands for team if you get paged:
```
# check nat SNAT errors
kubectl -n infra exec -it nat-metrics -- curl localhost:9100/metrics | grep snat

# check stream tail latency
curl -s "https://observability/api/query?metric=stream_handshake_p99&region=eu-west-2" | jq .
```
Use those to triage quickly.

mike (neteng): new tcpdump after scale shows fewer retransmits and SYN/ACK RTT stabilized ~120-200ms for most flows. still a small percentage at ~800-1.2s — those map to a single AZ pair (azb->azd). investigating cross-AZ routing table.

sophia (platform): rolling routing table diff now. suspect route flapping between azb/azd for specific subnet. running `ip route get` checks.

jessica: streaming proxy canary at 50% shows p99 down to 450ms. progressing to 100%.

raj (oncall): decision: keep nat-gw scale + port range change for next 2 hours; traffic shift to eu-west-1 to remain at 20% for 30m then re-evaluate. notifying SRE and support and logging runbook actions.

carla: support note updated: "Mitigation applied: additional egress capacity and partial regional failover. Expecting latency to normalize; continue to open tickets if you see >1s handshake."

mike (neteng): root-cause hypothesis: ephemeral port exhaustion combined with intermittent cross-AZ route instability producing delayed retransmits -> increased TLS handshake tail. working with cloud provider on routing flap cause.

raj (oncall): timeline to share:
- t0 (5179998888): alert fired for p99 handshake > 1200ms
- t+3m: SNAT port pressure observed
- t+8m: nat-gw scale + port range bump initiated
- t+12m: traffic shift 20% to eu-west-1 started
- t+18m: measurable p99 improvement to ~450ms; canary passed

jessica: moving to post-incident follow-up: we'll keep this thread open for root-cause with neteng and infra. please add any correlation logs (conntrack dumps, provider BGP events).

mike (neteng): collecting conntrack snapshot and provider peering logs; will upload link. initial note: provider shows brief control-plane flap between azb/azd at t+5m which coincides with worst tails.

sophia (platform): reversing canary traffic shift after 30m window once carrier confirms stability. will file infra change to increase nat capacity automatically in future when snat_in_use > 80% for 1m.

carla: leaving a short customer-facing postmortem draft in docs for review. will wait for root-cause confirmation before sending final.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: mitigations applied, monitoring. severity -> Sev2 (customer impact limited, no data loss).

raj (oncall): thanks all — great rapid coordination. if anyone hits this thread with new findings, drop them here. I'll escalate to platform lead if provider confirms persistent routing flaps.
